title: Conformer: Convolution-augmented Transformer for Speech Recognition

citations.claim: Gulati et al. proposed the Conformer, which combines self-attention for capturing global interactions with depthwise convolutions for extracting local features, achieving state-of-the-art speech recognition on LibriSpeech.

The Conformer architecture demonstrated that combining convolution and self-attention modules within a single block captures both local and global dependencies more effectively than either mechanism alone.

Gulati et al. showed that Transformers are effective at modeling long-range global context but less capable of extracting fine-grained local feature patterns, while CNNs effectively exploit local information through position-based kernels.

The Conformer uses a macaron-style sandwich structure with two half-step feed-forward layers surrounding a multi-headed self-attention module and a convolution module, connected by residual connections.
Gulati et al. employed relative sinusoidal positional encoding from Transformer-XL, which allows the self-attention module to generalize better across different input lengths.
The Conformer achieved word error rates of 2.1%/4.3% on LibriSpeech test/testother without a language model, and 1.9%/3.9% with an external language model.
Gulati et al. found that depthwise convolution kernel sizes of 17 to 32 yielded the best performance, with larger kernels (65) causing degradation.

do_not_claim: The Conformer was designed for or applied to signal separation or baseline correction tasks
The Conformer uses algorithm unrolling or learned iterative optimization
The Conformer was applied to chromatographic or spectroscopic data
